title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

SUNRPC: fix netns use-after-free in write_gssp()

While fuzzing with...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

SUNRPC: fix netns use-after-free in write_gssp()

While fuzzing with a customized syzkaller, I hit a refcount warning in
xprt_alloc(), reached from a write to /proc/net/rpc/use-gss-proxy:

  refcount_t: addition on 0; use-after-free.
  WARNING: lib/refcount.c:25 at refcount_warn_saturate+0xf8/0x120
  CPU: 0 PID: 10404 Comm: syz.0.17 Not tainted 7.3.0-rc1-00096-gcfebfd3db73d
  Call Trace:
   <TASK>
   xprt_alloc+0x83f/0x9d0
   xs_setup_xprt+0xaf/0x3c0
   xs_setup_local+0x47/0x7f0
   xprt_create_transport+0x16c/0x730
   rpc_create+0x38e/0x7f0
   gssp_rpc_create+0xe2/0x180
   set_gssp_clnt+0xba/0x1b0
   write_gssp+0x200/0x310
   proc_reg_write+0x240/0x330
   vfs_write+0x2aa/0x1050
   ksys_write+0x12a/0x250
   do_syscall_64+0x117/0x750
   entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f
   </TASK>

create_use_gss_proxy_proc_entry() stores the struct net pointer as the
proc entry's private data without taking a reference on it, and an open
file descriptor does not pin the namespace either, as procfs only pins
the proc_dir_entry. write_gssp() reads that pointer back with
pde_data() and hands it to set_gssp_clnt(), which reaches xprt_init():

	xprt->xprt_net = get_net_track(net, &xprt->ns_tracker, GFP_KERNEL);

get_net_track() -> get_net() -> refcount_inc() is unconditional, so
rpc_create() assumes its caller holds a reference on args.net.
write_gssp() does not.

Dropping the last ns.count reference does not make the file go away.
__put_net() only queues cleanup_net() on a workqueue, and the
remove_proc_entry() that fences off further writes runs from the
rpcsec_gss pernet .exit method, that is, from inside cleanup_net(). A
write landing between those two points increments a refcount that is
already zero. cleanup_net() does not re-read ns.count, so the namespace
is freed anyway and the rpc_xprt -- along with the AF_LOCAL socket
opened for it -- is left pointing at freed memory. The resurrected
count is visible to the rest of that teardown too: with
CONFIG_IPV6_MROUTE the same cleanup_net() worker then trips
!mr_can_free_table() in ip6mr_free_table(), which tests check_net() on
the namespace it is freeing.

It reduces to opening /proc/net/rpc/use-gss-proxy inside a new network
namespace, calling setns() back to the original one to drop the last
reference, and then writing "1" to the still-open descriptor.

Take the reference in write_gssp() itself and refuse the write when the
namespace is already gone. This is what procfs does for every other
/proc/net file: get_proc_net() is maybe_get_net(PDE_NET(PDE(inode)))
and seq_open_net() returns -ENXIO when it fails. PDE_NET() cannot be
reused here because the parent directory /proc/net/rpc carries no
namespace pointer. Adding a .pre_exit to rpcsec_gss_net_ops so the
entry is removed earlier would only narrow the window, since pre_exit
also runs from cleanup_net().

Live namespaces are unaffected: a write still returns the error from
set_gssp_clnt(), a write of "2" still returns -EINVAL, and reads are
untouched.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

RDMA/uverbs: Fix DMABUF use-after-free during ufile cleanup

The DMA...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

RDMA/uverbs: Fix DMABUF use-after-free during ufile cleanup

The DMABUF release can race with ufile cleanup. When the cleanup holds
hw_destroy_rwsem for write, uverbs_uobject_release() fails its trylock
and leaves the uobject on the ufile list, but the dma_buf is freed as
soon as the release returns. The cleanup then destroys the uobject and
uses the freed dma_buf:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in uverbs_dmabuf_fd_destroy_uobj+0x46/0x200
  Read of size 8 at addr ff11000109cf14b0 by task repro/435
  Call Trace:
   uverbs_dmabuf_fd_destroy_uobj+0x46/0x200
   destroy_hw_fd_uobject+0x3f/0x50
   uverbs_destroy_uobject+0xc5/0x380
   __uverbs_cleanup_ufile+0x1a8/0x260
   uverbs_destroy_ufile_hw+0x54/0x160
   ib_uverbs_close+0x34/0x110
  Allocated by task 435:
   dma_buf_export+0x1b5/0x530
   ib_uverbs_handler_UVERBS_METHOD_DMABUF_ALLOC+0x223/0x3f0
  Freed by task 436:
   kfree+0x301/0x530
   dentry_kill+0x14c/0x560
   __fput+0x23a/0x4a0

rdma_user_mmap_entry_remove() dereferences the same pointer.

Protect the stored dma_buf pointer with a mutex and clear it before
release returns. Use a shared revoke helper so uobject destruction and
mmap entry removal both skip a cleared pointer. Hold a temporary uobject
reference across uverbs_uobject_release() and the pointer update.

Use a separate mutex because uobject destruction can free the mmap entry
before release finishes. Map and unmap use attachment->dmabuf directly,
so they do not need to take the new mutex while holding the reservation
lock.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/hugetlb: fix use-after-free in hugetlb_mfill_atomic_pte()

Let's ...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/hugetlb: fix use-after-free in hugetlb_mfill_atomic_pte()

Let's fix another instance where we use a folio after dropping the PTL,
where someone else could e.g., MADV_DONTNEED it once we drop the PTL,
making us trigger a use-after-free on the folio.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/hugetlb: fix use-after-free of a new anon folio

For a fault in a...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/hugetlb: fix use-after-free of a new anon folio

For a fault in a private mapping with nothing in the page cache,
hugetlb_no_page() allocates a folio, locks it and maps it.  The folio has
one reference, which belongs to the page table entry from then on.  After
dropping the page table lock the function still sets the migratable flag
of the folio and unlocks it.

Whoever zaps the entry in between frees the folio.  The fault holds the
fault mutex and the lock of the vma.  MADV_DONTNEED and the first unmap of
a hole punch, hugetlb_vmdelete_list(), do not take the fault mutex, and a
private vma only has a lock if it owns a reservation map: not with
MAP_NORESERVE, and not in the child after fork().

Then the flag is set in, and folio_unlock() is called on, a folio that is
free or has a new owner.  A surplus page goes back to the page allocator
while it is locked:

  BUG: Bad page state in process init  pfn:108e00
  flags: 0x200000000000059(locked|uptodate|dirty|head|node=0|zone=2)
  page dumped because: PAGE_FLAGS_CHECK_AT_FREE flag(s) set

A page of the pool can be given to the next user, of any file, who locks
it and loses the lock to the late folio_unlock():

  kernel BUG at mm/filemap.c:1532!
   hugetlb_no_page+0x111b/0x23e0
   hugetlb_fault+0x3a9/0x14a0

An unprivileged process is enough: threads that write to a MAP_PRIVATE |
MAP_NORESERVE hugetlb mapping, threads that call MADV_DONTNEED on it, and
one that takes the freed pages for another file.

Until commit 3a47c54f09c4 ("hugetlbfs: revert use i_mmap_rwsem for more
pmd sharing synchronization") the fault held i_mmap_rwsem for reading,
which everybody who zaps takes for writing.  The lock that commit
bf4916922c60 ("hugetlbfs: extend hugetlb_vma_lock to private VMAs") gave
to private vmas closed the window again, but only for those with a
reservation map.

Be done with the folio before the page table lock is dropped, as
hugetlb_wp() is with its copy.  The function already unlocks page cache
folios under that lock.

Original fix generated by an LLM and sent in private by Josef.

[david@kernel.org: simplify+move comment]

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: emux: Fix UAF of soundfont zones at note-on

snd_emux_note_on(...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: emux: Fix UAF of soundfont zones at note-on

snd_emux_note_on() looks up the matching zones via
snd_soundfont_search_zone(), which takes sflist->lock only during the
lookup and returns the raw zone pointers after releasing it.  The
caller then stores them in vp->zone without any protection.
Meanwhile, a concurrent SNDRV_EMUX_IOCTL_REMOVE_LAST_SAMPLES ioctl may
unlink and free those zones in snd_soundfont_remove_unlocked(); this
leads to a use-after-free in snd_emux_note_on(), and later at
accessing the cached vp->zone, e.g. in snd_emux_send_effect().

Fix it by holding sflist->lock in snd_emux_note_on() over the whole
zone lookup and voice setup, and let snd_soundfont_search_zone()
require the caller to hold the lock, instead.
snd_soundfont_lock_preset() takes sflist->lock for setting
presets_locked, so the removal path now syncs with the note-on finish.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/panthor: Fix TOCTOU race between GROUP_REGISTERED check and eras...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/panthor: Fix TOCTOU race between GROUP_REGISTERED check and erase

panthor_group_destroy() checks the GROUP_REGISTERED mark and then calls
xa_erase() without holding the xarray lock across both. If the handle is
destroyed by another thread in between, and a concurrent GROUP_CREATE
reuses the freed ID, the first destroy erases and releases the new,
still-initializing group, leading to a use-after-free in
panthor_group_create().

Do the mark check and erase atomically under xa_lock().

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

filelock: keep superblock active through delegation wait

A caller m...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

filelock: keep superblock active through delegation wait

A caller may drop its path after try_break_deleg() returns a delegated
inode but before break_deleg_wait() finishes. The extra inode reference
held in struct delegated_inode does not keep the superblock active.

After a lazy unmount, closing the delegation holder can release the last
mount reference and shut down the superblock while another task waits for
the delegation break. The waiter's final iput() can then enter the
filesystem's eviction code after its superblock-private state was freed.
This has been observed as a KASAN use-after-free in shmem_evict_inode().

When try_break_deleg() saves a delegated inode, take an active reference
to its superblock while the caller still pins the mount. Keep that
reference through break_deleg_wait() and the final iput(), then release
it with deactivate_super(). This protects every caller of the helpers,
including the mknod, mkdir, symlink and rmdir paths that drop their path
before waiting.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fs/proc/task_mmu: pin mm_users in do_pagemap_scan()

The PAGEMAP_SCA...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fs/proc/task_mmu: pin mm_users in do_pagemap_scan()

The PAGEMAP_SCAN ioctl takes mmap_read_lock() on an mm obtained from
/proc/<pid>/pagemap without holding a reference to mm_users.

proc_mem_open() deliberately grabs only mm_count, so a consumer that
touches the address space has to call mmget_not_zero() first.  Every other
consumer in this file does -- m_start(), do_procmap_query(),
show_smaps_rollup() and pagemap_read() -- but do_pagemap_scan() does not.

Without that reference the target can reach exit_mmap() concurrently, and
exit_mmap() calls unmap_vmas() while holding mmap_lock only for reading,
which does not exclude the scanner.  For ordinary VMAs this is harmless,
as free_pgtables() and remove_vma() run afterwards under mmap_write_lock. 
A shared hugetlb VMA is different: __hugetlb_zap_end() frees the VMA's
hugetlb_vma_lock inside the read-locked phase.

walk_hugetlb_range() can therefore load vma->vm_private_data, have the
lock freed underneath it, and then down_read() a freed rw_semaphore.  The
load happens before the freeing side clears the pointer, so this is a
use-after-free and not a NULL dereference.  Any unprivileged user can
reach it with no huge pages configured, as hugetlb_reserve_pages()
allocates the lock before the VM_NORESERVE early return.

Pin mm_users across the scan, the way the other consumers do.  mmput()
from the exiting task can then no longer reach exit_mmap() while a walk is
in progress.

[akpm@linux-foundation.org: remove unneeded & undesirable test for !mm]

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: pfncache: use a dedicated invalidation sequence for cache refre...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: pfncache: use a dedicated invalidation sequence for cache refresh

The gfn_to_pfn_cache refresh path guards against mmu notifier
invalidations which complete while it has dropped gpc->lock for the
HVA->PFN lookup: hva_to_pfn_retry() samples kvm->mmu_invalidate_seq
and retries if it changed, or if mn_active_invalidate_count is still
elevated.

That is insufficient for HVA-based caches. mmu_invalidate_seq is only
advanced by kvm_mmu_invalidate_end() when the invalidated range
overlaps a memslot, and an HVA-based cache (e.g. the Xen shared_info
page mapped with KVM_XEN_ATTR_TYPE_SHARED_INFO_HVA) need not be backed
by any memslot at all. An invalidation of the cached HVA which starts
and ends entirely within the lookup window is thus invisible to the
retry check: mn_active_invalidate_count is back to zero and the
sequence never moved. The refresh then publishes a mapping of a page
which has already been freed, and the next reader dereferences it:

  BUG: KASAN: use-after-free in kvm_xen_shared_info_init+0x3c6/0x440
  Read of size 4 at addr ffff8880599c2900 by task syz.2.383/7257

Since gfn_to_pfn_cache_invalidate_start() deliberately skips caches
which are not currently valid (including one whose refresh is in
progress, as the refresh clears the valid flag before dropping the
lock), the retry check is the only line of defence, and it must fire
for *any* invalidation, not just those hitting a memslot.

Add a dedicated kvm->gpc_invalidate_seq, incremented by every
kvm_mmu_notifier_invalidate_range_end() under mn_invalidate_lock
before mn_active_invalidate_count is decremented, and check it in
hva_to_pfn_retry() instead of mmu_invalidate_seq. Incrementing in
range_end() in the same critical section as the in-progress count
also closes the variant where the cache is activated with the
contested HVA only after invalidate_range_start() has run.

The same bug is also reachable through the per-vCPU vcpu_info cache
(KVM_XEN_VCPU_ATTR_TYPE_VCPU_INFO_HVA), where the stale mapping is
then dereferenced by kvm_setup_guest_pvclock() on the next KVM_RUN:

  BUG: KASAN: use-after-free in kvm_setup_guest_pvclock+0x5bf/0x660

This intentionally makes refresh retry on *unrelated* mmu notifier
events; restoring precision (and reworking the GPC locking more
generally) is left for a subsequent series.

Reproducers: https://david.woodhou.se/xen_shinfo_race.c
             https://david.woodhou.se/vcpu_info_race.c

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: PPC: Book3S HV: Add SRCU protection for virtual-mode HPT hcalls...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: PPC: Book3S HV: Add SRCU protection for virtual-mode HPT hcalls

The virtual-mode HPT hcall handlers (H_ENTER, H_REMOVE, H_BULK_REMOVE,
H_CLEAR_REF, H_CLEAR_MOD) call into book3s_hv_rm_mmu.c, which accesses
memslots via kvm_memslots_raw().  kvm_memslots_raw() uses
rcu_dereference_raw_check() to bypass SRCU lockdep annotation checking.
This is safe in real mode because the entire guest entry/exit is wrapped
in srcu_read_lock/unlock inside kvmppc_run_core() and
kvmhv_run_single_vcpu().

However, since commit 6165d5dd99db ("KVM: PPC: Book3S HV: add virtual
mode handlers for HPT hcalls and page faults"), these same handlers are
also executed in virtual mode via kvmppc_pseries_do_hcall(), which runs
after SRCU has already been released on guest exit.

A concurrent KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION deletion or move can therefore
call synchronize_srcu_expedited() — which does not wait for this thread —
and then kfree(slot) and vfree(slot->arch.rmap) while the hcall handler
still holds a raw pointer to the memslot.  lock_rmap() then writes to
freed vmalloc memory, leading to use-after-free and memory corruption.
Because kvm_memslots_raw() suppresses lockdep checks, this race is
entirely silent.

Fix this by factoring out the 7 HPT hcall handlers (H_REMOVE, H_ENTER,
H_READ, H_CLEAR_MOD, H_CLEAR_REF, H_PROTECT, H_BULK_REMOVE) into a
helper function, kvmppc_pseries_do_hpt_hcall(), and wrapping its call
site in srcu_read_lock(&kvm->srcu) / srcu_read_unlock(&kvm->srcu, idx).
Targeting only the HPT hcalls avoids wrapping non-HPT hcalls that sleep
(such as H_CONFER, H_REGISTER_VPA, H_PAGE_INIT) or handlers that already
acquire SRCU internally (such as H_RTAS).

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/rmap: don't discard lazyfree THPs at PMD level

__discard_anon_fo...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/rmap: don't discard lazyfree THPs at PMD level

__discard_anon_folio_pmd_locked() clears a lazyfree THP's PMD before it
determines whether the folio can be discarded, and restores it if the
folio is dirty or has extra references.  It is done under only the PMD
lock and the anon_vma read lock inside try_to_unmap_one() and no mmap lock
is held.  The temporarily none PMD causes UAF.

A parallel munmap() or mremap() is supposed to serialize with it on the
PMD lock, but zap_pmd_range() (called by munmap()) and move_page_tables()
(called by mremap()) do not take the lock when they see the temporarily
none PMD and skip the PMD.  There is no more page table walk after the
none PMD is restored:

- munmap(): free_pgtables() waits in unlink_anon_vmas() for the anon_vma
  lock, then free_pmd_range() drops the restored PMD as bad without
  removing the rmap, so the folio keeps a stale mapcount.

- whole-VMA MREMAP_DONTUNMAP: dontunmap_complete() unlinks the source VMA
  from its anon_vma while the restored PMD still maps the folio.

- plain mremap(): the THP is not moved but unmapped, so the THP's data is
  lost.

In the first two cases, the folio stays mapped, but no VMA that maps it is
linked to its anon_vma.  When the anon_vma is freed, it is still reachable
when one rmap walks the folio.  Racing lazyfree reclaim against
MREMAP_DONTUNMAP as an unprivileged user reproduces a KASAN use-after-free
in folio_lock_anon_vma_read() as reported in the Closes link.

One solution is to use an invalidated PMD instead of a cleared one until
the discard is committed, but it needs arch fixes first.
1. GUP-fast still follows an invalidated PMD on riscv, LoongArch and s390.
2. sparc64 miscounts thp_pte_count when an invalidated PMD is set again or
   cleared.

To keep the fix simple for backport, stop discarding lazyfree THPs at PMD
level instead. try_to_unmap_one() splits the PMD and discards the folio at
PTE level.

unmap_huge_pmd_locked() and __discard_anon_folio_pmd_locked() are left in
place, unused, to minimize this fix for backport and the invalidated PMD
approach is planned as a follow-up series to use them again.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/truncate: look up the end-edge straddler by index

In truncate_in...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/truncate: look up the end-edge straddler by index

In truncate_inode_partial_folio(), after the first split at the start
edge, folio_split() unlocks and drops the refcount of the after-split
sub-folios.  The sub-folio straddling the end of the truncation range is
therefore unlocked and only transiently ref'd in the page cache while the
code still derives it from a page pointer inside the original folio.

Between the first split finishing and page_folio() resolving split_at2,
that tail page can be reclaimed, freed and reallocated as a new large
folio in the same mapping at a different file offset.  folio2 then points
at a folio that does not cover the end boundary, yet folio2->mapping ==
folio->mapping still holds, so the stale pointer passes the mapping check
and folio_split_or_unmap() splits a folio at a wrong position (or, with a
transient refcount, a use-after-free window opens between try_get and the
split).  __folio_split()'s own folio != page_folio(split_at) check cannot
catch this either since split_at2 has been reallocated as part of the new
folio, so page_folio(split_at2) resolves back to folio2.

Look the straddler up by its page index instead.  __filemap_get_folio()
returns the folio currently covering the boundary, ref'd and locked, with
the mapping validated under the lock, so the split target is always the
real folio at the end edge.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: sched: prevent scheduling deactivated qdiscs

TAPRIO can schedu...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: sched: prevent scheduling deactivated qdiscs

TAPRIO can schedule a deactivated qdisc after some_qdisc_is_busy() has
reported it idle.

Commit 47e8dbb6e763 ("net/sched: do not reset queues in graft operations")
made graft deactivation skip queue reset, leaving TAPRIO's timer armed.

A late callback schedules NET_TX softirq work, whose dequeue path can
race the unlocked child-queue reset in taprio_reset(). The same skb can
be queued for deferred freeing by RTNL and dequeued for transmission.
In the reproducer, the TAP reader frees it before __rtnl_unlock() reads
its next pointer. KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free in
__rtnl_unlock+0xa3/0xd0, with a read of size 8 from the freed skb.

Reject deactivated qdiscs in __netif_schedule(). Callers' RCU protection
lets the existing grace period join earlier scheduling calls before the
busy check. Restart nonempty transmit queues on reactivation so suppressed
scheduling does not strand packets.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ufs: use u64 for directory size in ufs_last_byte

ufs1_read_inode() ...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ufs: use u64 for directory size in ufs_last_byte

ufs1_read_inode() and ufs2_read_inode() copy the untrusted 64-bit
on-disk size into inode->i_size.  ufs_last_byte() then truncates that
value to an unsigned int before calculating the valid extent of a
directory folio.

A directory size of exactly 4 GiB is truncated to zero.  In
ufs_find_entry(), subtracting the requested record length from that zero
forms an endpoint almost 4 GiB beyond the mapped folio.  A crafted UFS2
image produces:

  BUG: KASAN: use-after-free in ufs_find_entry+0x583/0x6e0 [ufs]
  Read of size 1
  ...
  ufs_find_entry
  ufs_inode_by_name
  ufs_lookup
  __lookup_slow
  path_lookupat

The KASAN classification reflects that the adjacent physical page was
free; the source-level operation is an out-of-folio read.  A controlled
UFS1 test with CONFIG_UFS_FS_WRITE enabled also made ufs_find_entry()
return a directory entry from an adjacent anonymous page.  unlink() then
passed that pointer to ufs_delete_entry(), which cleared the adjacent
page's 3
2-bit d_ino.  This write result reproduced three out of three
times.

UFS normally requires a privileged mount path.  A relevant boundary is
a privileged automounter or image-processing service handling an
attacker-supplied filesystem.  The write primitive additionally requires
UFS1 to be mounted read-write with CONFIG_UFS_FS_WRITE enabled; the read
is reachable with read-only UFS2.

Keep the intermediate size arithmetic at 64 bits so non-final pages are
bounded at PAGE_SIZE.  With this change, the same controlled tests reach
the real on-disk directory entry and produce no adjacent-page write or
KASAN report.  A reproducer and full validation logs are available on
request.

The vulnerable helper is present in v7.2-rc3, v7.1, v6.18.38, v6.12.95,
v6.6.111, and upstream master at 1229e2e57a5c.  Runtime reproduction and
fix validation were performed in an x86-64 QEMU guest running v7.2-rc3
with generic KASAN.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: pin refcount trees before dropping the lookup lock

A refcoun...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: pin refcount trees before dropping the lookup lock

A refcount tree returned to ocfs2_lock_refcount_tree() must stay alive
until that caller releases its operation reference. However,
ocfs2_get_refcount_tree() returns the cached pointer after dropping
osb_lock, and the caller only takes its kref afterwards. The registry
reference does not protect this gap from concurrent removal.

This can happen when another node frees a refcount root and reuses its
block with a different generation while this mount retains the old
cached tree. Two local operations on different inodes sharing the new
root, such as data CoW and an external xattr update, can then look up
the same stale tree. Their inode locks are independent, and both the
REFCOUNT DLM lock and rf_sem are acquired after the first operation
reference.

The following ordering is possible, with no other operation references:

  Data CoW                         Xattr update
  --------                         ------------
  Look up the old tree under
    osb_lock, then drop osb_lock
                                   Look up the same tree and take a kref
                                   Acquire the tree locks and read the
                                     new on-disk generation
                                   Erase the old tree under osb_lock
                                   Unlock and drop the operation kref
                                   Drop the registry kref, freeing tree
  Take a kref through the
    freed tree pointer

The final kref_get() accesses freed rf_getcnt storage, and subsequent
accesses in ocfs2_lock_refcount_tree() also use the freed allocation.

Take the operation reference in ocfs2_get_refcount_tree() before
releasing osb_lock, including when an insertion loses to another lookup.
Removal must acquire the same lock, so it cannot drop the registry
reference before the lookup has pinned the tree. Keep the existing
unlock and error path puts. The two callers that already hold the
refcount tree lock keep their borrowed lookup behavior and do not
acquire an extra reference.

KASAN report as below:

    BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in ocfs2_lock_refcount_tree+0x94a/0x9b0
    Read of size 4 at addr ffff888117212820 by task python3/497

[Kernel and hardware identification omitted.]

    Call Trace:
     <TASK>
     dump_stack_lvl+0x93/0xd0
     print_report+0xce/0x630
     ? ocfs2_lock_refcount_tree+0x94a/0x9b0
     ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5
     ? __virt_addr_valid+0x20e/0x420
     ? ocfs2_lock_refcount_tree+0x94a/0x9b0
     kasan_report+0xe0/0x110
     ? ocfs2_lock_refcount_tree+0x94a/0x9b0
     ocfs2_lock_refcount_tree+0x94a/0x9b0
     ? __pfx_ocfs2_lock_refcount_tree+0x10/0x10
     ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5
     ? ocfs2_refcount_cow+0x3b6/0xd90
     ? srso_alias_return_thunk+0x5/0xfbef5
     ? __kmalloc_cache_noprof+0x28d/0x610
     ? ocfs2_refcount_cow+0x3b6/0xd90
     ocfs2_refcount_cow+0x410/0xd90
     ? __pfx_ocfs2_refcount_cow+0x10/0x10
     ? __pfx___might_resched+0x10/0x10

     ? __pfx_ocfs2_inode_unlock+0x10/0x10

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: hold a reference on the parent in readdir

Listing a directory ...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: hold a reference on the parent in readdir

Listing a directory on an overlay uses a freed dentry and crashes the
kernel when a lookup moves the directory at the same time.

Code that can sleep may only use d_parent without a reference while
something stops a move of the dentry. ovl_iterate_real(),
ovl_need_adjust_d_ino() and ovl_cache_update() use the d_parent of the
listed directory and hold only the lock of that directory. When a
lookup finds the directory under another parent after a change to a
layer, d_splice_alias() moves it without that lock and drops its
reference on the old parent.

With a delay in ovl_iterate_real(), getdents64 on an overlay directory
raced a rename in the lower layer and a lookup that moved its dentry,
and after an rmdir of the old parent KASAN reported a use-after-free in
security_inode_getattr().

Fix this by using dget_parent() in the three functions.

[amir: fix comments in ovl_need_adjust_d_ino()]

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: set OVL_WHITEOUTS before publishing the upper dir

Listing a di...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: set OVL_WHITEOUTS before publishing the upper dir

Listing a directory while it is copied up causes a use-after-free of
the readdir cache.

A merge directory must never be iterated as a real upper directory:
that mode frees the cache in OVL_I(inode)->cache without looking at
its refcount, while files opened in merged mode still use it.
ovl_copy_up_workdir() publishes the upper dentry before it sets
OVL_WHITEOUTS, and ovl_dir_open() samples both without a lock, so an
open between the two stores finds the upper directory and takes it
for a real one.

With a delay between the two stores, an unprivileged process that
listed a directory during its copy-up saw only "." and "..", and its
next getdents freed the readdir cache of another descriptor.

Fix this by setting OVL_WHITEOUTS before ovl_inode_update(), so that
ovl_dir_reset() agrees with ovl_dir_open(), and by testing
OVL_TYPE_MERGE() of the path type in ovl_dir_open(), so that an open
that observes the upper dentry never iterates a merge dir as a real
dir, regardless of the order in which it observes the flag.

[amir: test OVL_TYPE_MERGE() instead of smp_rmb() in ovl_dir_open()]

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: use the pinned upper dir in ovl_fix_origin()

Renames made dire...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: use the pinned upper dir in ovl_fix_origin()

Renames made directly on the upper filesystem during a lookup crash the
kernel.

A dentry that is passed to vfs_setxattr() must be pinned.
ovl_fix_origin() passes upper->d_parent to ovl_set_impure() without a
reference, and the lookup holds no lock of the upper directory. A
rename on the upper filesystem changes d_parent, and only the child
pins the new parent, so a second rename and an rmdir free it.

With delays in ovl_fix_origin() and ovl_set_impure(), renaming the upper
directory twice and removing the intermediate parent during the lookup
of a merge directory without an origin xattr gave a KASAN
use-after-free in vfs_setxattr().

Fix this by passing the upper dentry that the overlay parent holds.

[amir: add helper ovl_set_impure_dir()]

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: reject out-of-range attribute value lengths in xfs_attr_copy_va...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: reject out-of-range attribute value lengths in xfs_attr_copy_value

xfs_attr_copy_value() takes the value length as a signed int and, for a
remote xattr, is handed args->rmtvaluelen.  That field is filled from the
on-disk __be32 xfs_attr_leaf_name_remote.valuelen in
xfs_attr3_leaf_getvalue(), so a crafted length such as 0x80000000 is
stored into the signed rmtvaluelen as a negative number.

The "buffer too small" guard in xfs_attr_copy_value() is a signed
comparison:

	if (args->valuelen < valuelen)
		return -ERANGE;

A negative valuelen therefore compares as smaller than the caller's
buffer size, skips the -ERANGE path, and is then used as a copy length,
leading to an out-of-bounds copy of a full remote block into a small
getxattr(2) buffer on a mounted crafted image.

Reject a value length that is negative or larger than the maximum xattr
size before it is used, so a bogus on-disk length can no longer slip
through the value copier.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: reject remote xattr entries with an out-of-range value length

...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: reject remote xattr entries with an out-of-range value length

xfs_attr3_leaf_verify_entry() validates a remote attribute entry's name
but never bounds its on-disk value length (xfs_attr_leaf_name_remote.
valuelen, a __be32). A crafted leaf with valuelen = 0x80000000 passes
the verifier and the CRC.

That length is later assigned into the signed int args->rmtvaluelen
(xfs_attr3_leaf_getvalue), becoming negative, which slips past the signed
-ERANGE check in xfs_attr_copy_value(); a getxattr() with a small buffer
then memcpy()s a full remote block into the small kvalue buffer
(xfs_attr_rmtval_copyout) -- a heap out-of-bounds write with
attacker-controlled content, from an unprivileged getxattr(2) on a
mounted crafted image.

Reject remote entries whose value length exceeds XFS_XATTR_SIZE_MAX in
the leaf verifier, so the malicious block is rejected at read time.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: bound inode fork length against the fork size during log recove...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: bound inode fork length against the fork size during log recovery

xlog_recover_inode_commit_pass2() copies an inode log item's data/attr
fork region into the inode buffer using the on-log region length without
bounding it against the fork capacity, e.g.:

	len = item->ri_buf[2].iov_len;
	memcpy(XFS_DFORK_DPTR(dip), src, len);

The only guard is an ASSERT, which is a no-op on production kernels
(CONFIG_XFS_DEBUG off), and xfs_dinode_verify() runs only after the copy.
A crafted image with a dirty log can therefore drive a heap out-of-bounds
write at mount time. The XFS_ILOG_DBROOT sibling already passes
XFS_DFORK_DSIZE as a bound; the DDATA/DEXT and ADATA/AEXT memcpy paths
did not.

Bound each logged fork region against the destination fork size before
copying it, and reject the log item with -EFSCORRUPTED when it does not
fit. Because the recovered inode is only verified after the fork data has
been copied in, the checks are done up front, before any memcpy into the
on-disk inode.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: nSVM: Reject KVM_SET_NESTED_STATE if L1 has EFER.LMA=1 && EFER....
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: nSVM: Reject KVM_SET_NESTED_STATE if L1 has EFER.LMA=1 && EFER.LME=0

Reject KVM_SET_NESTED_STATE if the incoming L1 host state has what is
effectively an impossible EFER combination of LMA=1 but LME=0, i.e. if the
state says long mode is active but not enabled.  Unlike VMX, SVM doesn't
have an explicit consistent check for the illegal combination; presumably
hardware simply ignores EFER.LMA if EFER.LME=0.

Unfortunately, KVM doesn't ignore EFER.LMA in this case and consumes the
illegal state when constructing the shadow MMU for L2.  E.g. if userspace
also clears CR4.PAE, then kvm_calc_cpu_role() will compute a role with 4 or
5 levels of paging, but shadow_mmu_init_context() will wire up the MMU to
use the paging32 template, which maxes out its levels at 2.

Note, the "real badness" is effectively the same as what happened with the
nVMX bug fixed by commit 112e66017bff ("KVM: nVMX: add missing consistency
checks for CR0 and CR4").  Unfortunately, the sanity check added by commit
72e2fb24a0b0 ("KVM: x86/mmu: Bug the VM if a vCPU ends up in long mode
without PAE enabled") doesn't work for this case, since L2 state is active
at the time of the page fault, but it's L1 that has the bad state.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Take SRCU in kvm_zap_gfn_range()

kvm_zap_gfn_range() walk...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Take SRCU in kvm_zap_gfn_range()

kvm_zap_gfn_range() walks memslots and rmaps and may drop mmu_lock to
reschedule. Callers that do not already hold kvm->srcu (or slots_lock)
can race with memslot deletion: synchronize_srcu_expedited() does not
wait, kvm_free_memslot() frees the old slot and its rmap, and the zap
resumes on freed memory.

The VFIO noncoherent-DMA path hits this by zapping the entire GPA
space without SRCU. KASAN reported:

  BUG: KASAN: vmalloc-out-of-bounds in slot_rmap_walk_next+0x82/0x1c0
  Read of size 8 at addr ffffc900005c1008
  Call Trace:
   slot_rmap_walk_next+0x82/0x1c0
   __kvm_rmap_zap_gfn_range+0x17a/0x280
   kvm_zap_gfn_range+0x2a6/0x6a0
   kvm_vfio_set_attr+0x576/0x770
   kvm_device_ioctl+0x1ff/0x3b0

Take SRCU inside kvm_zap_gfn_range() so every caller is covered.
Nesting with an existing kvm->srcu critical section is fine; the
helper uses a local index. Drop the now-redundant SRCU pair from
__kvm_set_or_clear_apicv_inhibit().

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: hwdep: Serialize DSP load requests

The check of the loaded DS...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: hwdep: Serialize DSP load requests

The check of the loaded DSP indices and the call of the driver's
dsp_load callback in snd_hwdep_dsp_load() are not serialized.  A hwdep
file descriptor can be shared among threads, or inherited across fork,
so two SNDRV_HWDEP_IOCTL_DSP_LOAD requests for the same index can both
observe the index as unloaded and enter the driver's callback
concurrently, even though the device itself is opened exclusively.

This breaks the assumption behind hw->dsp_loaded that a firmware index
is loaded only once.  For example, snd-usb-usx2y hits
WARN_ON(usx2y->as04.buffer) in usx2y_async_seq04_init() and may
allocate the US-428 sequence URBs twice.

Serialize the check, the callback invocation and the bookkeeping with a
per-hwdep mutex, so that the second request returns -EBUSY.

title: llama.cpp GGUF File Parsing Heap-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability.
summary:
llama.cpp GGUF File Parsing Heap-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of llama.cpp. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of GGUF files. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a heap-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-34558.

title: The Coder VS Code extension opens Coder workspaces in VS Code with a single click.
summary: The Coder VS Code extension opens Coder workspaces in VS Code with a single click. From 0.1.20 until 1.14.6, a malicious repository can provide .vscode/settings.json values for security-sensitive Coder settings because the extension permits workspace and folder scope to override those settings. Values such as coder.headerCommand and coder.tlsCertRefreshCommand are later executed as shell commands, while other affected settings can redirect the Coder CLI binary or download source, inject CLI or SSH flags, replace TLS material, disable TLS verification, or change identity and credential-storage behavior. A victim with the extension installed must open the malicious workspace or repository; when the extension activates, attacker-controlled commands can run with the victim user's privileges. The issue also affects untrusted workspaces because the extension declares untrusted-workspace support without preventing consumption of the workspace-controlled settings. This issue is fixed in version 1.14.6.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fbdev: udlfb: don't rebuild the mode list while the framebuffer is in use

dlfb_setup_modes() frees info->modelist with fb_destroy_modelist() and
rebuilds it, but fbcon holds raw pointers into that list in
fb_display[i].mode and nothing un-publishes them the way
do_unregister_framebuffer() and store_modes() do with
fbcon_delete_modelist(). The function does refuse to install a new mode
while the framebuffer has users (dlfb->fb_count != 0), but only after the

an unprivileged write to /sys/class/graphics/fb0/edid therefore fails with
-EINVAL and still leaves every fb_display[i].mode dangling; the next
console switch reads the freed fb_videomode in fb_videomode_to_var().

fbcon_open(), so that condition covers exactly the states in which
fb_display[] points into the list, and the errno returned to userspace is
unchanged.

title: A vulnerability has been identified in Rexroth IndraWorks.
summary: A vulnerability has been identified in Rexroth IndraWorks. This flaw allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the user’s system by parsing a manipulated file, because the file parser fails to properly sanitize the path name(s) or references embedded in the manipulated file. Exploitation requires user interaction, specifically opening a specially crafted file, which then causes the application to traverse outside the target directory and to write files in unauthorized locations, eventually enabling Remote Code Execution (RCE). This can lead to a complete compromise of the system running Rexroth IndraWorks.

title: In the vulnerability-lookup web application, the authentication decorators for feed-key requests (auth_feedkey_func in website/decorators...
summary:
In the vulnerability-lookup web application, the authentication decorators for feed-key requests (auth_feedkey_func in website/decorators.py) and API-key requests (auth_func in website/web/api/v1/common.py) called Flask-Login's login_user() function. This caused the HTTP response to a request authenticated solely by a feed key (supplied as the X-FEED-KEY URL parameter) or an API key (supplied as the X-API-KEY header) to set a session cookie that grants full authenticated access to every page in the application, without requiring a password or two-factor authentication.

The practical impact is that any party possessing a leaked feed URL (a common occurrence, as feed URLs are shared with RSS readers) or an API key could obtain a valid web session for the associated account. This session provides access to the user's account page, which exposes the API key and other profile data, and for accounts with the administrator role, access to the /admin interface, enabling full administrative control of the application.

The vulnerability affects all users whose feed key or API key is exposed. No prior authentication, user interaction, or special network conditions are required; a single HTTP request with the token is sufficient to establish the session. The session persists until it expires, and because it is not bound to the original credential (a related CWE-613 issue noted by the developers), revoking the feed key or API key does not invalidate the already-created session.

The fix replaces the login_user() call with assignment to g._login_user, which Flask-Login's current_user property reads for the current request only, without writing any session cookie. The affected views remain unchanged and continue to see the authenticated user for the single request.

summary: LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. title: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems.
summary: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 2.1.0 until 4.5.2, get_eacontent in libatalk/vfs/ea_ad.c subtracts MAX_REPLY_EXTRA_BYTES from a client-controlled FPGetExtAttr MaxReplySize without rejecting values from 1 through 5, and a signed-to-unsigned comparison can then select an untrusted AppleDouble ea_size. An authenticated client on a volume configured with ea = ad can use a pre-existing malformed AppleDouble sidecar to make read copy attacker-controlled bytes beyond dsi->data + 6 into the surrounding struct DSI, including protocol callback pointers. The malformed sidecar must already exist or be created through a separate local, co-export, management, restore, or vulnerability-assisted write path, and practical code execution depends on the target architecture, structure layout, and address uncertainty; runtime command execution was demonstrated on one x86-64 build. Volumes using ea = sys, ea = none, or ea = auto when it resolves to native system xattrs do not reach this path. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.2.

summary: A flaw was found in the Kuadrant WebAssembly (WASM) shim shipped in Red Hat Connectivity Link 1.5. title: PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass via algorithm downgrade.
summary:
PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass via algorithm downgrade.

The Phar extension selects the signature verification method from the signature type stored in the archive, and only the OpenSSL types consult the separate .pubkey file holding the trusted public key. An attacker who can modify an OpenSSL-signed Phar archive, but not its public key file, can switch the signature type to a keyless hash such as SHA-256 with a recomputed digest, so the altered archive passes verification even with phar.require_hash enabled. An application that loads the archive may then execute attacker-controlled PHP code. Native, tar-based and zip-based phars are affected.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

The following description summarizes the vulnerability reported via our Penetration Testing program:

Crucible do not account for path parameters when validating protected paths requested through the static-resource route. A crafted path segment passes validation, after which Jetty removes the path parameter during dispatch and resolves the request to a protected resource. This can expose files under WEB-INF and permit direct invocation of admin-area JSPs outside the normal interceptor and administrative password checks. An ordinary authenticated user can exploit the issue, and unauthenticated exploitation is possible when anonymous access is enabled.

title:
Issue summary: When an application passes a stack to
PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() to add entries to, and reading fails,
OpenSSL frees ever...
summary:
Issue summary: When an application passes a stack to
PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() to add entries to, and reading fails,
OpenSSL frees every entry in the stack, both the old ones and any new
ones, but leaves them in the stack.

Impact summary: An application that passes an existing stack to
PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() and keeps using it after a failed read may
use memory that was already freed. This can cause a crash or, in
principle, memory corruption. Malformed PEM data can make the read fail,
but only applications that pass an existing stack are affected, and
OpenSSL itself does not do this.

CWE: CWE-416: Use After Free

Description: PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() reads certificates, CRLs and
private keys from PEM data and adds them to a stack of X509_INFO
structures. If the application passes a stack that is not NULL, the
function adds the new entries to it and must leave the entries that are
already there unchanged.

If reading fails, the function frees every entry in the stack. This
includes the entries that were there before the call, and the entries
added by the call. It does not remove these entries from the stack, so
the stack keeps pointers to freed memory. The failure can happen at any
point, even before any entry was added. A PEM item with invalid content
is enough.  This also happens if the stack was empty: entries added
before the failure are freed but stay in the stack.

An application that then reads or frees the stack will use memory that
was already freed. This can crash the application or, in principle,
corrupt memory.

Only applications that pass a stack that is not NULL are affected.
OpenSSL itself never does this. Its own callers, including the code that
TLS uses to load CA certificates, always pass NULL. When the stack is
NULL, the function frees only the entries that it created itself, which
is safe. We expect that very few applications pass an existing stack. An
attacker can make the read fail with malformed PEM data, but cannot make
an application pass an existing stack.

The same problem affects PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio(), PEM_X509_INFO_read()
and PEM_X509_INFO_read_ex(), which use the same code. OpenSSL 1.1.1 and
1.0.2 have only the first two of these functions.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

title: A flaw was found in KServe.
summary: A flaw was found in KServe. A namespace-scoped user with create/update permissions on InferenceService custom resources can exploit this vulnerability by providing a malicious `storageUri`. This Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability allows the `storage-initializer` init container to issue arbitrary outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from inside the cluster. This can lead to information disclosure, including credential theft for the node's Identity and Access Management (IAM) role or access to internal cluster services.

title: SportEase is a web application for managing school sports events, class rosters, and competition teams.
summary: SportEase is a web application for managing school sports events, class rosters, and competition teams. Prior to 1.3, an authenticated account with is_profile_complete=false can submit an attacker-selected class_id for any class in the currently active event to PUT /api/user/profile during first profile completion. AuthHandler.UpdateProfile accepts the class without validating the user's legitimate membership and automatically derives and assigns the corresponding {class_name}_rep role while isFirstCompletion is true. The attacker can become representative of one selected class, view roster information including email addresses, and add or remove competition-team assignments. Downstream handlers correctly reject access to other classes, so the impact is bounded to the selected class, but the representative privilege cannot be revoked through the exposed API and requires direct database intervention or another out-of-band remediation method. This issue is fixed in version 1.3.

title: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), multi-factor authentication (MFA) is not enforced on the PEM web application's own routes.
summary:
In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), multi-factor authentication (MFA) is not enforced on the PEM web application's own routes. An attacker who knows the password of a user who has enrolled a second factor can skip the second factor and call PEM's pages and APIs directly, with that user's permissions. A similar issue in pgAdmin 4 was assigned CVE-2024-4215.
From PEM 10.6.1, every authenticated PEM route requires a completed MFA check.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

batman-adv: tt: ignore ROAM flag of received ADD changes

A received...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

batman-adv: tt: ignore ROAM flag of received ADD changes

A received TT change (OGM diff or full table response) with the ROAM flag
but without DEL is handled by batadv_tt_global_add() like a ROAMING_ADV:

* a newly created global entry gets BATADV_TT_CLIENT_ROAM and is
  therefore excluded from the global CRC. The sender has it in its local
  CRC and the receiver has to request the full table again
* batadv_tt_global_purge_local() removes the local entry of the
  receiver. The receiver's own client is considered as roamed to the sender
  and frames for it are rerouted

The ROAM flag only has a meaning together with DEL. Drop it on reception to
keep it from populating the global table with a temporary ROAMING entry
which is not part of the CRC - and therefore causing a CRC mismatch.

title: In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to view an affected container could query the Representational...
summary:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to view an affected container could query the Representational State Transfer (REST) API for approvals to retrieve a live external prompt link belonging to another user. Using this link, the user could read the approval prompt without authentication and submit a response, potentially disrupting or altering the automated workflow governed by that approval.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API for approvals exposes the live external prompt link without verifying that the requester owns the approval.

title: In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could store malicious S...
summary:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could store malicious Search Processing Language (SPL) in a shared dashboard. The malicious SPL could run using the permissions of the user who opened the dashboard and could access or modify data available to that user and disrupt Splunk Enterprise availability.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not preserve quoted search argument boundaries when it processes a dashboard search.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the affected user by tricking them into initiating a request within their browser. The attacker, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role, should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.

title: In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could add attacker-cont...
summary:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could add attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) to a shared dashboard. When another user opens the dashboard in Splunk Web, Splunk Enterprise could run the attacker-controlled SPL using the permissions of that dashboard viewer. The attacker-controlled SPL could expose stored credentials, modify indexed data, and reduce availability.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not neutralize special elements in search filter values before it builds optimized search jobs.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the affected user by tricking them into initiating a request within their browser. The attacker should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.

title: In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could craft a shared Cl...
summary:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could craft a shared Classic Dashboard that runs arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands for another authenticated user. Exploitation requires the dashboard viewer to open the shared dashboard. The injected commands could access data available to the dashboard viewer, modify data available to the dashboard viewer, and partially disrupt Splunk Enterprise.
For more information see Add sparklines to search results (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/search/search-manual/10.6/calculate-statistics/add-sparklines-to-search-results), Configure dashboard permissions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/create-dashboards-and-reports/simple-xml-dashboards/10.6/manage-and-share-dashboards/configure-dashboard-permissions), and SPL safeguards for risky commands (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/best-practices-for-splunk-platform-security/spl-safeguards-for-risky-commands) in the Splunk documentation.

title: In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could create and share ...
summary:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could create and share a metric alert that causes Analytics Workspace to run a malicious Search Processing Language (SPL) when another authenticated user opens a link to the alert. The malicious SPL could expose data, modify data, or disrupt services available in the affected session. 
The vulnerability is possible because Analytics Workspace does not fully neutralize metric alert names before including the names in SPL.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the user by tricking them into opening a link that the attacker creates. The user who holds the "power" Splunk role should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see Alerts in the Analytics Workspace (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/create-dashboards-and-reports/analytics-workspace/10.4/using-the-analytics-workspace/alerts-in-the-analytics-workspace) and Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.

title: United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP Backend Configuration Hard-Coded Credentials Authentication Bypass Vulnerability.
summary:
United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP Backend Configuration Hard-Coded Credentials Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the configuration of the OCPP backend settings interface. The issue results from the use of hard-coded credentials. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29056.

title: Vulnerability in the Oracle Hyperion Financial Close Management product of Oracle Hyperion (component: Reconciliation Manage).

title: This High severity Improper Authorization vulnerability was introduced in versions 10.2.0, 11.0.0, 12.0.0, and 12.1.0 of Bamboo Data Center.
summary:
This High severity Improper Authorization vulnerability was introduced in versions 10.2.0, 11.0.0, 12.0.0, and 12.1.0 of Bamboo Data Center.

This Improper Authorization vulnerability, with a CVSS Score of 7.6, allows an unauthenticated attacker to gain unintended access and can lead to the exposure of resources or functionality, possibly providing attackers with sensitive information or even execute arbitrary code.

Atlassian recommends that Bamboo Data Center customers upgrade to latest version, if you are unable to do so, upgrade your instance to one of the specified supported fixed versions:
 Bamboo Data Center 10.2: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 10.2.26

 Bamboo Data Center 12.1: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 12.1.13

 Bamboo Data Center 13.0: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 13.0.1

See the release notes ([https://confluence.atlassian.com/bambooreleases/bamboo-release-notes-1189793869.html]). You can download the latest version of Bamboo Data Center from the download center ([https://www.atlassian.com/software/bamboo/download-archives]).

This vulnerability was reported via our Penetration Testing program.

title: The SMSC911x/LAN9220 Ethernet driver stages every outgoing frame in a fixed-size static buffer before pushing it to the controller FIFO.
summary:
The SMSC911x/LAN9220 Ethernet driver stages every outgoing frame in a fixed-size static buffer before pushing it to the controller FIFO. eth_tx() in drivers/ethernet/eth_smsc911x.c took the frame length from net_pkt_get_len(pkt) and passed it directly to net_pkt_read(pkt, tx_buf, total_len), with no comparison against the size of tx_buf (NET_ETH_MAX_FRAME_SIZE). net_pkt_read() takes no destination size and only fails when the packet is shorter than the requested length, so any packet longer than the staging buffer was copied past its end.

Nothing between the IP layer and the driver bounds the frame to what the link can carry: ethernet_send() in subsys/net/l2/ethernet/ethernet.c performs no length check, and the IPv6 output path only compares the packet against the interface MTU when CONFIG_NET_IPV6_FRAGMENT is enabled (it is disabled by default). The size the stack will build is therefore governed by the interface MTU, and that MTU is remotely settable: handle_ra_input() in subsys/net/ip/ipv6_nbr.c honours the MTU option of any Router Advertisement with a value up to 0xffff, gated only by the standard hop-limit-255 and link-local-source checks. An unauthenticated attacker on the same link can raise the MTU and then have the device emit a single frame of several kilobytes, for example as a TCP segment from any service that returns more than ~1.5 KB or as an oversized UDP datagram.

The result is an out-of-bounds write into .bss immediately after tx_buf, with the overrun length and much of its content derived from the transmitted frame. Consequences range from corruption of adjacent kernel data and a crash to potential control-flow influence where the clobbered globals hold pointers; the practical overrun size is bounded by the network buffer pool rather than by the advertised MTU. The fix rejects frames larger than NET_ETH_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with -EMSGSIZE before any TX_DATA_PORT write, so the controller FIFO is also not left holding a command word without its payload.

The residual bytes become the next DSI header, allowing protocol desynchronization that can close sessions, corrupt protocol state, or trigger an infinite-read denial of service. sctp_init_caus...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sctp: account for chunk padding in sctp_init_cause()

sctp_init_cause() accepts a chunk when skb_tailroom() can hold the
cause header and the payload. sctp_addto_chunk() then writes 0-3
bytes of padding before that header so the chunk stays 4-byte
aligned. The check does not include the padding, and the following
skb_put() calls skb_over_panic() from softirq.

Count the padding sctp_addto_chunk() is about to write. The cause
length on the wire stays the header plus the payload.

Found by LLM inspection, triggered and tested the fix.

summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvme-rdma: fix NULL queue->ctrl dereference on reconnect

Since commit 2a8513091d2f ("nvme-rdma: parallelize I/O queue allocation
and startup"), a reconnect that gets more I/O queues than before grows
the tag set before the new queues are set up. queue->ctrl is only set
by nvme_rdma_setup_io_queues(), so I/O submitted in between reaches
nvme_rdma_queue_rq() on a queue that was never allocated and
dereferences a NULL queue->ctrl:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 000000000000034c
  RIP: 0010:nvme_rdma_queue_rq+0x52/0xb90

Set queue->ctrl for every queue when allocating the controller. Such
requests are then requeued like on any other queue that is not live.

summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: cap the block count of xfs_iomap_write_direct() at one extent

xfs_iomap_write_direct() reserves blocks for the whole count in an
unsigned int. For a pNFS layout the client chooses that count, and an
RW LAYOUTGET for 16 TiB wraps the reservation and shuts XFS down.

xfs_bmapi_write() maps at most XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN blocks here, so cap
the count at that. nfsd asks again for the rest. The other callers get
the same mapping as before.

summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvmet: don't return memory contents beyond valid data when reading ANA log page

The host side does not know how much valid data will be returned by the target
so it will typically provide a buffer larger than the amount of valid data in
the ANA log page.  The memory allocation used by the target does not guarantee
that prior kernel memory contents will not be returned past the end of the valid
page data.  Fix this to ensure that the SGL is zeroed before copying the data.

title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unbounded arc length in OBJECT IDENTIFIER decoding and encoding.
summary:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unbounded arc length in OBJECT IDENTIFIER decoding and encoding.

The content of an OBJECT IDENTIFIER or RELATIVE-OID element is passed to unpack "w*" on decode, and the arcs of an OID string to pack "w*" on encode. Perl converts each arc to or from its decimal string in time quadratic in the arc's length, and nothing limits that length.

An attacker who controls the decoded data, or an OID string passed to encode, can exhaust CPU with a single oversized arc.

title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via a declared element length passed unchecked to sysread in asn_read...
summary:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via a declared element length passed unchecked to sysread in asn_read and asn_get.

The length an element declares in its BER header is passed to sysread as the read size. Perl grows the target buffer to that size before reading, so memory is allocated from the declared length, not from the data received. A 6-byte header can declare a length of up to 4GB.

A single header makes the reading process allocate the declared size. Where the allocation fails, perl exits with "Out of memory", which eval cannot catch.

title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unlimited recursion depth in constructed-form string decoding.
summary:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unlimited recursion depth in constructed-form string decoding.

Any constructed-form string element causes the decoder to recurse on the element's contents. The BER encoding controls nesting depth at four bytes per level, with no bound checked. Perl recursion is heap-allocated, so the process grows without a stack crash.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust memory with a small deeply nested constructed string.

title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via zero-length BIT STRING content.
summary:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via zero-length BIT STRING content.

A BIT STRING with zero content octets passes -1 to substr as the length. Perl reads a negative length as an offset from the end of the string, so the decoded value is nearly all of the input that follows the element. In the constructed form each zero-length segment copies the rest of the input again, so memory grows with the square of the input size.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust memory with a short constructed BIT STRING. The resulting value also contains bytes from adjacent input.

title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via exponent-notation string in INTEGER encoding.
summary:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via exponent-notation string in INTEGER encoding.

The encoder routes any value with abs >= 2**31 to i2osp without validating that it is an integer. A string in exponent notation such as "1e8000" passes that threshold. Math::BigInt expands it to an 8001-digit integer, and i2osp's per-octet conversion loop is quadratic in that size.

An attacker who controls encoded INTEGER values can exhaust CPU with a short exponent-notation string.

title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unchecked exponent length in binary REAL decoding.
summary:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unchecked exponent length in binary REAL decoding.

Binary REAL decoding never bounds-checks the exponent length against the available content. For a minimal one-byte binary REAL, the exponent byte is read from outside the element, making the mantissa length -1. Perl reads a negative length as an offset from the end of the string, so the mantissa is nearly all of the input that follows the element. The long-form exponent path also omits the extra length octet when sizing the mantissa.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust CPU with a list of such values, as each mantissa loop iterates over the remaining input. The decoded values are also computed from bytes outside each element.

title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded MSG_PEEK buffer doubling in asn_recv.
summary:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded MSG_PEEK buffer doubling in asn_recv.

asn_recv peeks the socket in a loop, doubling the buffer size on each pass until a tag and length can be decoded. An inverted boolean guard ($tb || rather than $tb &&) prevents the need-more-data exit from firing once a tag byte has been decoded. When asn_decode_length returns no value because the length is absent or incomplete, no exit fires for that case either. MSG_PEEK leaves socket data unconsumed, so each re-peek returns at once while the buffer size doubles.

A single truncated BER header sent to a process calling asn_recv doubles the peek buffer until memory is exhausted. Perl's realloc failure is fatal and not catchable with eval.

title: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via quadratic bigint loop in os2ip.
summary:
Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via quadratic bigint loop in os2ip.

Every INTEGER or ENUMERATED longer than four content octets reaches os2ip, which iterates over each content octet with $result = ($result * 256) + $octet. Each multiplication operates on a bigint that grows by one octet per step, so decoding an n-octet value takes O(n^2) bigint work. Nothing limits content length before this loop runs.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust CPU with a single oversized INTEGER or ENUMERATED value.

title: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty.
summary: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldSection in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java loops while fieldSectionLength is nonzero and relies on disabled-by-default assertions to require BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine to return a value and consume bytes. A corrupt field line can consume more bytes than its understated declared section length and drive the counter negative, or a truncated field line can return without consuming data and leave the parser in the same state. An unauthenticated OHTTP peer can encrypt such Binary HTTP content under the gateway public configuration, reach OHttpRequestResponseContext.ContentDecoder.decodeChunk, and permanently pin a Netty event-loop thread at full CPU before application business logic. Multiple requests can exhaust the event-loop group and deny service until restart. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

title: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty.
summary: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java treats a complete field line that ends exactly at a known field-section boundary as incomplete and returns without consuming bytes. BinaryHttpParser.readFieldSection then leaves fieldSectionLength unchanged and repeats the loop because its forward-progress checks are Java assertions, which are normally disabled in production. A remote peer that sends a known-length Binary HTTP header or trailer section ending at that boundary can make the parser spin indefinitely and pin the Netty event-loop or worker thread responsible for the channel. title: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server.
summary: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.0.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, a WebSocket upgrade that is pipelined behind another HTTP request on the same cleartext connection arrives while that request's response is still attached to the socket. The shared upgrade listener sees the socket is already claimed and returns early without taking the upgrade, but it does not attach an error listener to the raw socket, and Node.js has already removed its own error listener before emitting the upgrade event. A later socket error on that connection, such as a client connection reset, is therefore unhandled and terminates the Node.js process. A single unauthenticated connection that pipelines an upgrade behind a normal request and then resets is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. Upgrades over TLS are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

title: RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository.

The target must mirror an upstream repository controlled by the attacker, and the default "Check GPG signatures" option triggers the vulnerable call. The command executes before a later signature-verification failure, so a valid signed package is not required. Fixed in 5.13.3.

title: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server.

Building the upstream target then throws, the error is only logged, and the accepted client socket is left open with no error listener, so the next frame the client sends becomes an unhandled error and terminates the Node.js process. A request target that is not a valid URL reference reaching a parameterized prefix triggers the same path. A single unauthenticated upgrade request followed by one frame is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

title: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server.
summary: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.0.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, it takes every upgraded socket and dispatches the request through the Fastify router before the WebSocket library takes ownership of the socket. Node.js removes its own error listener from the socket before emitting the upgrade event, and the plugin does not attach one of its own during routing, so a socket error such as a client connection reset that arrives before the WebSocket library takes over is unhandled and terminates the Node.js process. The error window is open whenever anything asynchronous runs between dispatch and the route handler, such as an async hook on the proxied route or any unrelated async route in the application. A single unauthenticated upgrade request followed by a connection reset is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.
